_readonly_uri (sql_runner.py:65-84) has three branches: Windows drive -> 'file:///C:...', path starting '//' -> 'file://'+path (yields 'file:////...' with empty authority), otherwise 'file:'+path (no '//'). Every output therefore has an empty or absent authority. I re-executed the function body in isolation for C:/x.db, //x/y.db, ///x, rel.db, UNC-like backslashes and special chars; none gave an authority, and sqlite3 returned only 'unable to open database file' for the missing files, never 'invalid uri authority'.

_WINDOWS_DRIVE = re.compile(r'^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]') (sql_runner.py:32) has no platform check, and _readonly_uri tests it first (line 78). So on POSIX 'C:/x.db' yields 'file:///C:/x.db?mode=ro' (verified by executing the function), whose URI path is /C:/x.db, not the relative file. The test test_readonly_uri_has_no_host pins this output.

'C:\\x.db' matches the drive regex ([\\/] class). The function then returns file:///C:%5Cx.db?mode=ro (verified by executing it), because quote(path[2:], safe='/') encodes the backslash as %5C. The 'may not treat as a separator on Windows' part is hedged and not contradicted by the code.
